defs.def: to fail to hit, catch, reach, etc. sth 未击中；未得到；未达到；错过

ex.s: I have missed plenty of beautiful sunsets/sunrises due to being on the spot only five minutes before the best moment.
ex.t: 由于只在最佳时刻前五分钟赶到现场，我错过了许多美丽的日落和日出。

ex.s: Asking about “the point” of ALife might be, well, missing the point entirely, he says.
ex.t: 询问ALife的"意义"可能——嗯——完全偏离了重点，他说。

ex.s: Short writings missed as a result of an excused absence will be accepted.
ex.t: 因准予缺勤而错过的短写作业将被接受。

ex.s: David had not missed a single practice, and although he always finished his run long after the other children, he did always finish.
ex.t: David没有错过一次训练，虽然他总是在其他孩子很久之后就完成了跑步，但他总是会完成。

ex.s: If you miss two PASS sessions in a row, you will be deregistered and your place will be given to someone on the waiting list.
ex.t: 如果你连续错过两次PASS课程，你将被取消注册，你的位置将给候补名单上的人。

ex.s: they give their places to othersD. they miss two sessions in a row
ex.t: 他们把名额让给别人 D. 他们连续错过两次活动

ex.s: Of course, connecting passengers don’t want to miss their flights.
ex.t: 当然，转机的乘客不想错过航班。

ex.s: are anxious about missing their flights

ex.s: After a short way, the farmer stopped and pointed at a weed which we missed.
ex.t: 走了一小段路后，农场主停下来，指着我们漏掉的一株杂草。

ex.s: It went missing.
ex.t: 它失踪了。

ex.s: I’ve missed the point
ex.t: 我错过了重点

ex.s: But Moore was sick of missing out on candies.
ex.t: 一切始于摩尔和她爸爸一起去银行的时候。

ex.s: When fat and salt     64     (remove) from food, the food tastes as if is missing something.
ex.t: 当脂肪和盐从食物中   64   （去除），食物尝起来像少了什么。

ex.s: If Tononi’s theory is right, it would explain why, when we miss a night’s, we find it harder the next day to concentrate and learn new information — our brains may have smaller room for new experiences.
ex.t: 如果托诺尼的理论是对的，就能解释为什么我们少睡一夜后，第二天更难集中注意力和学习新信息——我们的大脑可能为新体验留出的空间更小了。

ex.s: And at the end of the day, you won’t want to miss the view of the sun that is setting on the sea!
ex.t: 最终你不会想错过海面上落下的太阳的景象！

ex.s: You once missed a national dragon boat race because of injuries.
ex.t: 你曾因为受伤错过了一次全国龙舟赛。

ex.s: There's nothing wrong with this, but don't miss out on new experiences for fear of the unknown.
ex.t: 这本身没有什么问题，但不要因为害怕未知而错过新的体验。

ex.s: All kinds of human emotions are on display: sad (tearful goodbyes), happy (family get-togethers), anxious (waiting in a long line) and upset (missing a flight).
ex.t: 各种各样的人类情感都在展现：悲伤（含泪的告别）、快乐（家庭团聚）、焦虑（排长队等候）和沮丧（误了航班）。

ex.s: I often leave early to seek the right destinations so I can set up early to avoid missing the moment I am attempting to photograph.
ex.t: 我经常早早出发去寻找合适的目的地，这样我可以提前架好设备，避免错过我想拍摄的瞬间。

ex.s: Why did scientists miss this?
ex.t: 科学家为什么错过这个？

ex.s: Starring Anne Hathaway, it is definitely a movie you should not miss!
ex.t: 由安妮·海瑟薇主演，这绝对是一部你不应错过的电影！

ex.s: If you see humor as an optional form of entertainment, you’re missing some of its biggest benefits: Humor makes average-looking people look cute and uninteresting people seem entertaining.
ex.t: 如果你把幽默看作一种可有可无的娱乐形式，你就错过了它最大的好处之一：幽默让长相普通的人显得可爱，让无趣的人显得有趣。

ex.s: With so many online posts featuring the same places, it’s easy to feel like you’re missing out.
ex.t: 网上有那么多展示同一批地方的帖子，你很容易觉得自己错过了什么。

defs.def: to fail to hear, see or notice sth 未见到；未听到；未觉察
to fail to understand sth 不理解；不懂
to fail to be or go somewhere 不在；不去；错过
to fail to do sth 不做；错过
to not take the opportunity to do sth 错过机会

ex.s: It's a chance not to be missed.
ex.t: 这是个不容错过的机会。

ex.s: But once having met and liked them, we think how terrible it would have been, had we missed the chance.
ex.t: 但一旦我们遇到并喜欢上他们，我们就会想，如果错过了这个机会该有多糟糕。

ex.s: Miss the opportunity to succeed．
ex.t: C. 错过了成功的机会。

defs.def: to be or arrive too late for sth 迟到；赶不上；错过
to feel sad because you can no longer see sb or do sth that you like 怀念；思念

ex.s: The theater will be missed.
ex.t: 人们会怀念这家剧院的。

ex.s: “I’ll miss these old boats,” he said as we parted.
ex.t: "我会想念这些旧船的，"我们分别时他说。

ex.s: His research shows that this is often missing for people with mental health conditions.
ex.t: 他的研究表明，对于有精神疾病的人来说，这常常是缺失的。

ex.s: You’ll be informed by email if you are being deregistered as a result of missing sessions.
ex.t: 如果因缺席活动而被注销，你会收到邮件通知。

ex.s: “I’m going to miss you so much, Poppy,” said the tall, thin teenager.
ex.t: "我会非常想念你的，波比，"那个瘦高的少年说。

ex.s: “But as I grew older,” Adeline says, "and missed my brother more and more, I realized that was the only thing we had left." Corrado Piccoli’s Purple Heart medal now hangs at the Italian American Civic Association in Watertown.
ex.t: "但随着年龄的增长，"阿德琳说，"而且我越来越想念我的哥哥，我才意识到这是我们唯一留下的东西。"科拉多·皮科利的紫心勋章现在挂在沃特敦意大利美国公民协会。

ex.s: As    65    result, people will eat more food to try to make up for that something missing.
ex.t: 作为    65   结果，人们会吃更多食物，试图弥补缺失的那点东西。

defs.def: to notice that sb/sth is not where they/it should be 发觉丢失；发觉 … 不在原处

ex.s: Scents of the missing plants are preserved in the atmosphere.
ex.t: 森林和雪的气味变化有一个共同的潜在原因。

ex.s: The following day, called to the headmaster’s office, I found myself accused of stealing the missing parts.
ex.t: 第二天，我被叫到校长办公室，发现自己被指控偷了那些丢失的零件。

ex.s: Before hearing from Zac, Adeline hadn’t realized the medal was missing.
ex.t: 在收到扎克的来信之前，阿德琳并没有意识到勋章丢失了。

ex.s: have been missingD. will be missing
ex.t: 通过学会何时寻求帮助，我终于踏上了成为独立科学家的道路。

defs.def: to avoid sth unpleasant 避开（不愉快的事）

ex.s: I missed that paragraph because I was thinking of something else, but I’m going to keep on going and start paying close attention.”
ex.t: 我漏看了那一段，因为我在想别的事情，但我会继续读下去，并开始集中注意力。"

ex.s: At best, you may just find that you have discovered something completely new and unexpected, through a flash of inspiration that you would have missed with perfectionism.
ex.t: 往好了说，你或许会发现，通过一瞬灵感，你发现了某种全新而意外的事物——而若追求完美，你会与之失之交臂。

ex.s: How did Miss Chevalier succeed in making Addie truly understand the word “impetuous”?
ex.t: 谢瓦利埃小姐是如何让阿迪真正理解"impetuous"这个词的？

ex.s: Halfway through the poem, Miss Chevalier stopped me and asked if I knew what “impetuous” meant.
ex.t: 诗读到一半时，Chevalier小姐让我停下来，问我知道"impetuous"是什么意思吗。

ex.s: Miss Chevalier pretended not to have noticed my red face and handed me a dictionary, asking me to read its definition aloud.
ex.t: 谢瓦利埃小姐假装没注意到我涨红的脸，递给我一本字典，让我大声读出其中的释义。

ex.s: I read both definitions over again, trying to figure it out, but Miss Chevalier must have read my mind.
ex.t: 我把两个释义又读了一遍，试图弄明白，但谢瓦利埃小姐一定看穿了我的心思。

ex.s: After that, I would never call Miss Chevalier “Poodle” again.
ex.t: 从那以后，我再也不会叫谢瓦利埃小姐“贵宾犬”了。

ex.s: What can be learned about Miss Chevalier’s personality from the way she treated Addie?
ex.t: 从舍瓦利耶小姐对待艾迪的方式可以了解到她怎样的性格？

ex.s: What is the probable reason that Addie would never call Miss Chevalier “Poodle” again?
ex.t: 艾迪再也不会叫舍瓦利耶小姐“贵宾犬”的可能原因是什么？

ex.s: She was touched by Miss Chevalier’s trust.
ex.t: 离中心较远的地方住着平民和劳动者。

ex.s: She felt Miss Chevalier’s teaching funny.

ex.s: In that class, Miss Zhao, our biology teacher, showed we insects on stamps.
ex.t: 在那节课上，我们的生物老师赵老师给我们看了邮票上的昆虫。

ex.s: Miss Zhao told us the names of the insects or described their living habits.

ex.s: What does Miss Johnson want her students to become?

ex.t: “里姆小姐，”他叹了口气，“我想让你做，但如你所知，我们正处于战争之中。”

ex.s: I guess I was better than the others, for Miss Chevalier asked a while later, “Addie, I was wondering if you would recite the whole poem to the Saturday evening’s club.” She said a famous professor was going to give a lecture about the poet, and a presentation of that poem would be a fresh way to start.
ex.t: 我想我比其他人强一些，因为谢瓦利埃小姐过了一会儿问道："艾迪，我在想你是否愿意在周六晚上的读书会上把整首诗背诵出来。"她说一位著名教授将要做一个关于这位诗人的讲座，而朗诵那首诗会是一个新颖的开场方式。
